predecessors.name: Warring States Japan
predecessors.text: Bungo Province (Ōita Prefecture, which also holds the northern part of Buzen)

successors.name: Shimazu clan
successors.text: Bungo Province (Ōita Prefecture, which also holds the northern part of Buzen)

ledger.x: 1550: Sōrin's tenure begins; 'Funai Domain (Bungo)' inherited from his father.
1557: 'he defeated Akizuki Kiyotane and seized Chikuzen Province.'
1558: 'Mōri captured Moji castle from the Ōuchi'; in September 1559 Sōrin recaptured it but the Mōri 'quickly took the castle again'.
By 1569: 'Sōrin controlled Bungo, most of Buzen, Chikuzen, and Chikugo'.
1578: Sōrin 'sent captains into the Tsuchimochi area of Hyūga'.
10 December 1578: Mimigawa, a Shimazu victory; the Ōtomo lost several commanders and the Shimazu pursued survivors to the Ōtomo headquarters at Matsuyama castle.
1585: Horikiri Castle in Chikugo attacked, Iwaya Castle in Chikuzen taken; mid-1585 the Shimazu controlled both.
1586: the Shimazu 'seized Funai Castle from the Ōtomo'; Bungo fell after Hetsugigawa; the Sōrin page: the Shimazu 'defeated Sōrin at Battle of Hetsugigawa in 1586'.

wars.name: Ōtomo–Mōri war in Buzen
wars.outcome: Moji changed hands in 1558-1559; at Tatarahama in 1569 Sōrin forced the Mōri back and retook Tachibana castle.

wars.name: Battle of Mimigawa
wars.outcome: Shimazu victory on 10 December 1578; several Ōtomo commanders killed.

wars.name: Shimazu invasion of Ōtomo lands
wars.outcome: Horikiri and Iwaya in 1585; Tachibana and Funai in 1586; Bungo fell after Hetsugigawa; the Ōtomo appealed to Hideyoshi.

certainty.note: The pages name castles, provinces and battles, not borders; the Seven-Province Host included provinces only under influence, which are not drawn.
